replication.target_description: Replication of Stellar et al. Study 3: awe versus neutral video; humility as a strengths-to-weaknesses balance, plus individual strengths/weaknesses and reported-awe regression analyses.

n.sample_role: Participant-level analytic sample; exact target-test count is not explicitly stated.
n.exclusions: 94 participants completed the study, but zero weaknesses and subsequent ratios/log transformations caused analysis-specific exclusions. The source does not give final mutually exclusive group counts for these critical tests.
n.location: pp. 40–42, Participants, Results and Limitations; p. 45, Appendices D–E
n.quote: Ninety-four participants completed the study. ... the number of excluded observations varied across calculations. ... Computations including ratios or multiple log transformations specifically

notes: Identity verified from the supplied text: A Replication Study to Evaluate the Effects of Awe on Humility; Alexandra Bertrand, Jonah Kimmel, Salomé Duhamel, Héloïse Puel, Alexandra Schifano, and Émilie Wood; DOI 10.26443/msurj.v19i1.231; Research Article, Volume 19 Issue 1 April 2024, pp. 39–45. This is the primary replication report with methods, results, discussion, references and appendices A–G, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned unfinished fields were examined for completion; other side/fields are placeholders. Recruitment/completion N=94 is not accepted as analytic N. No N was inferred from degrees of freedom or ICC rater-pair observation counts; no final-group arithmetic is available. Target remains ambiguous: presentation of strengths and weaknesses can refer to their balance/humility t(69) = –0.34, p = 0.438, or to individual strengths t(91) = 0.85, p = 0.397 and weaknesses t(82) = 0.50, p = 0.618. Page 41 and Appendix E provide these separate tests. No outcome was selected and no analytic N was inferred from their differing df.
